thread:
carl: Heads-up — hit a weird latency/regression on m7b windows traffic after last kernel-selector tweak. p99 jumped from ~28ms -> ~57ms on long sliding-window sessions.

maya: ack. any logs/stacktrace? did the change touch RoPE scaling or seq_len thresholds?

carl: I pasted the kernel selector trace from a affected request: 
```
[kernelselector] seq_len=1536 choose=default_blk reason=seq>cfg.fast_max
[kernelselector] warmup_handoff -> kernel=matmul_opt at token=8
[kvcache] attach=sliding-window mode=wrap clamp_at=2048
```
Seems like we flip kernel during warmup and the KV pointer math for wraparound is getting misaligned.

lee: interesting — we recently changed the threshold to 1024->1200 to favor matmul_opt longer. maybe edge-case where we fallback back to default_blk mid-request due to kv-fragmentation.

anika: I profiled a representative trace and saw extra memcpy and mask recompute when kernel switches. short dump: p50 22ms, p95 39ms, p99 57ms vs baseline p99 28ms.

infra-bot: profile-uploaded: https://internal/profiles/1998765432/trace1

maya: could be RoPE scaling too — if we scale RoPE differently between kernels (we do implicit rescale for quant kernels), the sliding-window offset math can produce a mask that doesn't match cached KV indices. That forces re-encode of prefix and extra combiner ops.

tony: does this only affect m7b or also 8x7b?

carl: primarily m7b in this deployment because its head/kv dims end up with different kernel choices; 8x7b has different tiling and we haven't hit the threshold there yet.

lee: quick mitigation ideas: revert the threshold tweak, or prevent kernel handoff after token N (e.g., no handoff after warmup token 16). Also could clamp RoPE scaling to be identical between kernels to avoid mask drift.

anika: ran a canary where we disabled runtime kernel handoff (force matmul_opt for whole request) — p99 dropped back to 30ms. So kernel-handoff is the triggering action not the selector change alone.

maya: two-pronged fix: (1) guard kernel handoff to only occur at request boundary or token < warm_handoff_limit, (2) ensure RoPE scaling state is serialized into the KV layout & checked on attach to detect mismatches.

tony: also look at batching heuristic: I saw that the batch-slicer produces tail batches with mixed seq lengths which increases chance of mid-request kernel flip when autoscheduler re-evaluates. Might bump slice_coalesce so long-running sliding-window clients are kept in homogeneous batches.

carl: actionable plan: create a small patch that (A) blocks mid-request kernel handoff, (B) adds a KV attach sanity check comparing ropescale/version in cache header, (C) add a tiny batching heuristic tweak to keep sliding-window sessions grouped. I'll open PRs.

lee: please include a regression test that simulates wraparound max_position_embeddings boundary with switching kernels. simple harness should repro the misaligned mask and assert no extra mask-recompute operations.

anika: logging tip: when kernelselector flips, emit `kv_state_digest` (hash of positions + ropescale) so we can quickly see mismatches in logs.

carl: sounds good. I'll file the PRs and schedule a short canary run. thanks all :thumbsup:
